A Podcast by Tara AlSabban
(I) The Concept — الفكرة

Not everything is said in one language.

Shofa — شوفة, a glance — is a podcast for the generation raised between cities, languages, and inherited expectations. Hosted from London by Saudi creative Tara AlSabban, each episode is an unhurried conversation with artists, founders, designers, and thinkers rewriting what it means to belong to more than one place.

"A chaotic hustle that regenerated her faith in herself."

From fashion sets with Vogue to GCC social strategy, Tara has always worked at the seam where global culture meets Arab identity. Shofa is that seam, broadcast — the in-between made audible.

On the record A seat between two cities, two alphabets, two versions of self.

Meet the voice

The girl between two worlds.

Tara AlSabban is a London-based creative with Saudi roots and a distinct global perspective. Driven by a desire for more meaning and personal impact, she left a career in law for London's creative scene — a pivot she describes as "a chaotic hustle that regenerated her faith in herself."

Behind the scenes she has worked on high-profile shoots with Vogue and Defined Magazine, collaborating with talent including Chace Crawford, Emma Stone, Luke Newton, and Salma Hayek. She created youth content for Saudi audiences at Vice Media and now leads GCC social campaigns at a top London creator agency — blending strategic insight with cultural awareness.

Shofa is where that cross-cultural lens steps in front of the mic.
